title: [18/1/2023] The percentage of households with cars
prompt: The bar chart shows the percentage of households with cars in a European country between 1971 and 2001. Summarise the information by selecting reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart illustrates the proportions of households owning different numbers of cars in a European country over a 30-year period from 1971 to 2001.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, there was a clear shift in car ownership patterns during these three decades, with the proportion of households without cars declining steadily while those owning one or more vehicles increased. In addition, single-car ownership became the most common category after 30 years.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at households without cars and those with one vehicle, in 1971, approximately 45% of families did not own any cars, which was notably higher than the proportion having one car, at around 35%. Over the next three decades, the figure for car-free households decreased steadily to about 25% by 2001. In contrast, the percentage of single-car owners rose consistently, reaching its peak at roughly 52% in the final year.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding households with more than two cars, the proportion stood at about 25% in 1971. This figure then increased to approximately 35% in 1981, before fluctuating slightly and ending the period at a similar level of around 37%.
